title: DIODE-TOWER: two stacked transistors and 16-64 wrapped linear-capacitor tiers per pillar, steered by per-tier oxide Schottky diodes and read by a double-sampled in-hole gain FET
status_reason: No objection is fatal, and the engineering objections (plate RC, top of pillar, stack process, readout noise, coupling) all have priced redesigns: wrapped tier on Mo replacement plates, replacement-first flow, stacked 2T top, 300 um centre-driven segments, 0.3 V guard. The downgrade comes from three things. (1) The only contact class that met the barrier bar, AgOx, cannot survive the process, and no process-integrable anode (RuO2, MoOx, WOx) has an IGZO datum. (2) The bottom-anode interface (0.1-0.3 eV) and Poole-Frenkel/TAT leakage (+0.12-0.22 eV) could widen the barrier gap from 0.15-0.2 eV to 0.24-0.71 eV. (3) Once yield, per-tier and top-of-pillar costs are priced, $/bit at 64 tiers rises from 0.35x to 0.55x (about parity with a 2032 incumbent), the smallest step in the portfolio. EV falls from 45 to ~16 (S2 x P2 x D4). The concept stays alive as the two-terminal per-tier-device hedge, funded through the shared oxide coupon run until Gate A.

revised_verdicts.possible: Yes, conditionally, with lower confidence. No law is violated. It needs a process-integrable (RuO2/MoOx/WOx), bottom-anode, etch-back-formed contact at >=1.06-1.11 eV thick-film-equivalent, or 1.18-1.33 eV if Poole-Frenkel-limited, with sigma <= 0.05 eV in a 15 nm shell (budget 928 aA per ring at 85 C). No integrable anode has an IGZO datum; RuO2/IrO2 on GaN (1.43-1.48 eV) and Pd on a-HIZO (1.40 eV mean, but sigma 0.14 eV) show high barriers exist on wide-gap and amorphous oxides.
revised_verdicts.profitable: Density: ~3.9x 1-beta at 64 tiers (2.0x at 32; parity at 17). Bits/$: ~1.8x at 64 tiers ($/bit 0.55x at tier yield 0.995; 0.45x at 0.998, 0.76x at 0.99; 0.73x at 32 tiers). 2 transistors per 30-61 bits. Roughly parity vs a 2032 incumbent unless >=96 tiers at >=0.998. No energy step unless 1 s retention.
revised_verdicts.doable: Partly (less than before). A ~$260k Stage A ($170k without the bench) settles the diode on vertical-recess, ring-sized, bottom-anode coupons, plus RTN and drift, by M7. A 4-tier wrapped replacement-first stack fits a $960k / 24-month plan. Not provable inside $1M: >=32-tier yield, the AR >=30 replacement hole etch and the full-pitch stacked 2T top. P(pass) ~5-10% [ESTIMATE].

revised_experiment: Stage A (M0-7, $260k incl. a $90k reusable bench). Coupon matrix: process-integrable anodes only (RuO2 from a Ru node ring with in-situ O3 re-oxidation, MoOx, WOx, area-selective IrO2 liner) on 15-20 nm IGZO, Ga-rich IGZO and a-Ga2O3 shells, plus a Ga-free shell. Each anode runs bottom-anode as integrated vs a top-anode control on the same wafer, with a GaOx-interlayer split, under the cumulative <=400 C flow budget, with ToF-SIMS on passing splits. AgOx/PtOx/Pt are planar diagnostics only. Structures: (a) large diodes (diagnostic); (b) 1e4-1e6 ring-sized arrays; (c) >=1,000 (target 16k) diode-isolated floating nodes resolving 1e-19 A at 85-125 C, written and read at temperatures up to +/-60 K apart and re-tested over 1,000 h for time-varying leakage; (d) bipolar pulsed arrays to 1e12 pulses at ~1,100 A/cm2 with reverse-hold leakage re-measured every decade; NEW (e) 2-tier vertical recess coupons (SiO2/Mo/poly/Mo mold, 100-150 nm holes) with the real etch-back chemistry (+$30k). Missing measurement added: the 1e-4 RTN amplitude distribution on >=65k oxide gain FETs of <=0.01 um2 (L 50/100 nm) at 85 C with the design ~15 ns CDS gap, on the shared PIXEL-STACK / MARGIN STACK lot. Gate A, 2027-07-30, PASS: vertical-coupon 99.99th-percentile ring leakage <=928 aA at 85 C and 0.8 V; >=1.8 nA at <=1.2 V, 0 C, n<=1.3; delta-phi <=30 meV at 1e12 pulses; RTN tail <=25 mV (readout residual <=40 mV at 64-tier load). FAIL on any one of: all integrable splits >928 aA including the escape split; delta-phi >60 meV within 1e10; sigma >0.07 eV on every vertical coupon; RTN >50 mV at both lengths. Stage B (M7-20, $280k): a 4-tier wrapped stack in 100-150 nm holes built replacement-first (dielectric mold, sacrificial fill, Mo replacement, H bake, then in-hole stack) with the in-line access + gain 2T top on one merged bitline; a 32-pair mold bow coupon (<=150 um) and a replacement barrier-shift test (<=30 meV). PASS: margin >= the allowed residual at emulated 64-tier load, tail retention >=64 ms at 85 C, zero flips in 1e9 accesses including an adjacent-plate hammer, 1e12 cycles, HAR anode etch-back shown. Total plan $960k over 24 months (IP $55k, founders $300k, travel $15k, contingency $50k).

responses.response: Partly a units mismatch, but the substance holds. The dossier's 7 mV was an rms sigma, used as signal/2 >= 3.72 x 7.33 mV, i.e. ~26 mV of budget. PIXEL-STACK's 14.7 mV (24-35 mV after the RTN correction) is already a 3.72-sigma + RTN + coupling quantity, so '15 mV caps the tower at 14 tiers' maps one onto the other wrongly. Re-run in PIXEL-STACK units (sigma_SF 2.5 mV rms + deterministic 1e-4 RTN tail + 1.2 mV coupling): the back-wall cell reaches 79/52/39/22 max tiers at RTN 13/20/25/35 mV. 32 tiers survives a 20 mV tail; 64 tiers fails above ~13 mV, so the critic's conclusion holds for the 64-tier claim. The base cell is moved to the wrapped capacitor, made physical as Mo/poly/Mo with a 5 nm plate pull-back: Cs 0.594 fF (not 0.725), 65 nm tier, priced at $38/tier. It reaches 156/110/89/60 max tiers at the same RTN values; at 20 mV, z = 14.1 at 32 tiers and 8.3 at 64, and the allowed residual is 58/40 mV at 32/64 tiers. A longer in-hole gain FET is a further lever (RTN ~1/L, gate C ~L): 206 tiers at L = 100 nm. A bonded Si gain FET is not a real fallback at a 121 nm per-pillar pitch; it is replaced by a sequential Smart-Cut c-Si layer.
responses.action: Base = wrapped cell (model cell_wrap True, density/cost restated). G5 rewritten in PIXEL-STACK units: <=40 mV for 64 tiers, <=58 mV for 32. Add the 1e-4 RTN distribution on >=65k oxide FETs of <=0.01 um2 at 85 C with a ~15 ns CDS gap (L 50/100 nm splits) on the shared PIXEL-STACK/MARGIN STACK lot. New kill 6 at M9 (>50 mV at both lengths). Kill 11 rewritten (>58 mV kills; 40-58 mV caps at 32-48 tiers).

responses.response: The objection assumes data written at 85 C and read at 25 C. In this cell every read is destructive, and every refresh is a dump read plus a clamp write-back, so each level is re-written with V_f at the current temperature at least once per refresh interval. The write/read temperature difference is therefore bounded by die slew x interval, not by the +/-60 K range. Model: clamp V_f tempco 1.33 mV/K (1.10 eV contact, I_end). At 64 ms and 10 K/s (the LPDDR MR4-polling example rate [UNVERIFIED]), dT = 0.64 K and dV_f = 0.8 mV, giving a pillar offset of 0.28 / 0.19 mV at 32 / 64 tiers (0.4% of the half-margin). Even at 100 K/s the offset is 2.8 / 1.9 mV (4%). In 1 s refresh mode at 10 K/s it is 4.4 / 3.0 mV (6.6%). The critic's 60 K case (26 / 18 mV in the wrapped cell) needs data left unrefreshed while the die cools 60 K, which a DRAM never does. The reference tier is refreshed in the same interval, so it tracks too.
responses.action: Model now carries dV_f = slew x interval x tempco x Cs/(Cs+Cp) as a deterministic readout term. The coupon still writes and reads floating nodes at temperatures up to +/-60 K apart, to confirm the clamp tempco and the model. In 1 s (G2) mode the controller keeps the reference tier refreshed within the same interval.

responses.response: Reproduced. TiN 25 nm at ~150 uOhm.cm is 60 Ohm/sq; perforated by 101 nm openings at 121 nm pitch it is ~205 Ohm/sq (Maxwell-Garnett mesh). With ~0.23 fF of load per node, a 4-row segment has an Elmore delay of 4.0 ns at 50 um but 65 ns at 200 um. Keeping 50 um segments at 32 tiers needs 1.18M drivers/mm2 (0.85 um2 each) and 22% / 45% staircase overhead at 32 / 64 tiers: unworkable, as the critic said. Redesign: Mo replacement plates (25 uOhm.cm at 10 nm) in the wrapped tier. The two Mo layers are perforated only by the 60 nm hole (+5 nm pull-back), so the mesh is 21 Ohm/sq. With 8-row, 300 um segments driven from the centre, RC is 7.2 ns at the wrapped load (0.44 fF/node). That needs 0.10M drivers/mm2 at 9.6 um2 each, enough for a ~2 V thick-oxide driver or a NAND-style pass gate fed by global plate drivers. The page is ~19.8k pillars (2.4 KB). The staircase is now priced in density: 0.35 um/step per segment adds 3.7% / 7.5% at 32 / 64 tiers. Net density is 1.98x / 3.88x (was 1.94x / 3.94x), because 8-row slits halve the slit overhead.
responses.action: Model: rows_per_plate 4->8; seg_len_um 300 centre-driven; stair_step_um 0.35 in the footprint; new section 12b. A plate-driver/pass-gate floorplan is part of the M0-6 design work. Binary-chop multi-depth contacts are listed as the staircase-area reducer; the I-11544 Vt-coded decoder stays optional.

responses.response: Valid. Estimate for the back-wall cell: node k+1 sits directly above node k across 25 nm SiO2 + 2 x 5.5 nm ZrO2. Node-node coupling is 0.0045 fF (it follows plate k+1 at Cs/(Cs+Cj) = 0.95), and plate fringe adds up to ~0.01 fF. On a 0.284 fF node at a 1.9 V swing that is a 29-92 mV step, which eats up to half of the old 0.2 V guard on top of the 100 mV droop. Fixes: (1) guard 0.2 -> 0.3 V, which costs +0.1 V of plate swing (~1.9 V) and ~11% plate energy (plate term 2.3 fJ in a 31 fJ access); (2) in the wrapped tier plate k's own Mo layers lie above and below node k, shielding k +/- 1 to <= ~0.0005 fF (~2 mV) [ESTIMATE]. Guard left after droop: 108-171 mV back-wall, ~198 mV wrapped.
responses.action: m_rev 0.2->0.3 V in the model (hold bias 0.8 V propagated to all barrier bars). 3D TCAD extraction of plate/node-to-neighbour coupling at M0-1. An adjacent-plate hammer pattern is added to the M18 zero-flip test (kill 9).

responses.response: Agreed on the main point. Ag2O partly dissociates by 300 C and fully decomposes by ~400 C (PCCP 2001; RSC Adv 2012: stable in gas only below ~170 C), and Ag diffuses through thin oxides. AgOx was the only contact class at >= the 1.07 eV low-field bar, so its loss matters. AgOx moves to planar diagnostics only. One correction: in the hole flow all tiers are built in one sequence, so the anode sees IGZO ALD + core + top 2T + BEOL, one <=400 C budget rather than 32 tier anneals. The coupon will reproduce that cumulative schedule (IGZO ALD <=300 C, 2 x 350 C, 400 C 1 h), not one anneal. Consequence: the barrier gap is no longer '0.15-0.2 eV with a known contact class just above it'. It is 0.14-0.41 eV from the best IGZO datum of any kind (Pt, itself non-integrable), and no integrable anode has been measured on IGZO.
responses.action: Anode matrix restricted to RuO2 (Ru node ring, in-situ O3 re-oxidation), MoOx, WOx and an area-selective IrO2 liner, on IGZO / Ga-rich / a-Ga2O3 shells. ToF-SIMS on every G1-passing split. Cumulative thermal schedule. Downgrade: P 3 -> 2 (pass chance ~5-10% [ESTIMATE]), lowering provability, not the step-change if it works.

responses.response: Valid and supported: a JAP 2006 study of single-crystal ZnO Schottky diodes found reverse current dominated by Poole-Frenkel, with ~5x local field enhancement, and GaN reviews report PF + TFE. Deep V_O states in a-IGZO make the same likely. Model sensitivity (PF lowering = 2x the image-force term at the hold field): the G1 thick-film bar rises from 1.06-1.11 eV (thermionic) to 1.18-1.33 eV. A hypothetical 1.20 eV RuO2/IGZO contact goes from 0.56-2.6 s to 1-82 ms tail retention. A thick-film I-V-T / Werner-Guttler barrier therefore cannot down-select anodes. Field levers reduce PF too: the 20 nm shell bar is 0.99-1.02 eV thermionic, and the 80 nm escape geometry 0.97-0.98 eV.
responses.action: Gate A and the Q2 down-select are judged on measured ring-sized thin-shell leakage (structures b, c, and the new vertical coupons e) at 85 C / 0.8 V, plus its activation energy over 25-125 C. The critic's test (Ea = barrier, within 10x of thermionic) is reported as a diagnostic. The model adds the PF case (section 12f-g). Downgrade: worst-case bar +0.12-0.22 eV, folded into the P 3 -> 2 downgrade.

responses.response: Valid. Literature barriers come from O2-sputtered top contacts. Here IGZO ALD (metal-organics, H2O/O3, 150-300 C) grows on the anode and can strip interface oxygen; the a-RuOx/InAlN analogue falls from 0.75 to 0.55 eV after a vacuum anneal. The flip was evaluated: a pillar-core anode deposited last onto IGZO is a top contact and needs no anode etch-back, but it sits at the inner coaxial radius. Its hold field is 1.83 vs 0.91 MV/cm, costing +0.29-0.32 eV of image-force/TFE lowering at 60/15 nm (0.12-0.14 eV even at 100/20). That is as much as the 0.1-0.3 eV it avoids, so the flip is rejected. Process mitigations: in-situ O3 or O2-plasma re-oxidation of the Ru/RuO2 node face just before IGZO, O3-first low-temperature IGZO nucleation, and a 1-2 nm O3-ALD GaOx interlayer (DRAM's O3-ALD high-k on Ru electrodes is the analogue [UNVERIFIED]). If the 0.1-0.3 eV loss is real, the top-contact-equivalent bar is 1.16-1.41 eV (thermionic).
responses.action: Every anode is run as a pair on the same wafer: bottom-anode as integrated vs a top-anode control. This measures the penalty directly (gate G6), with a GaOx-interlayer split. The flipped variant is kept only as a planar diagnostic and disclosed in the IP (model 12h). Downgrade is part of the P 3 -> 2.

responses.response: Valid: noble-metal/IGZO interfaces switch through O-vacancy migration, so drift is a known mechanism. The wrapped cell makes the stress harsher: 29.7 nA average write, ~1,125 A/cm2, 1.1e-5 C/cm2 per pulse. Ten years of 64 ms refresh is 9.9e9 pulses, so a 1e12 test still covers it ~100x. The drift budget is unchanged: 30 meV = 2.6x leakage.
responses.action: G4 exactly as the critic asked: on the G1-passing anode at 85 C, with reverse-hold leakage re-measured every decade, using a bipolar waveform (forward pulses + 0.8 V reverse hold). Options: a 20 ns write (halves current density; V_f lower by kT ln2), Ga-rich shells and passivation against V_O migration, hot-row remap. Kill 3 unchanged (>60 meV within 1e10).

responses.response: Agreed. Kepler's 1T-nC stack (US 11423967/11527277/12096638) plus US 2007/0183191 (diode-accessed capacitor, other electrode on a plate line) is a credible two-reference obviousness case against delta #1 as a broad cell claim. Delta #1 is downgraded from 'looks new' to 'probably obvious'. The claim set moves to elements a combination does not teach and that are detectable: (a) single-pulse dump-read / clamp write-back through the steering diode plus the plate-swing rule (swing >= Vdata + V_f + guard), visible in plate/pillar waveforms; (b) the depleted-shell, outer-anode coaxial diode sized to an anode-field limit, with the flip shown inferior by +0.29-0.32 eV; (c) the wrapped Mo/poly/Mo recess tier with plate pull-back; (d) in-hole anode formation with interface-oxygen control. A moat issue, not physics.
responses.action: Read the claims of US 12096638 and US 2007/0183191 at M0-1 (+$10k counsel; IP line 45 -> 55k) before filing. Pre-1990 diode-capacitor search. FTO opinion moved ahead of stack 1. Dossier section 3 notes the downgrade of delta #1.

responses.response: Valid: a composition PASS is publishable and reproducible by anyone with in-hole oxide ALD, and the oxidised-metal-on-oxide Schottky is old art (US 8508015, AgOx 2008). What the company can own is the integrated cell, the operating method, and process steps detectable in a product (TEM/SIMS): an outer anode ring formed by etch-back + in-situ re-oxidation + O3-first oxide nucleation giving sigma <= 0.05 eV, the wrapped recess with plate pull-back, and the 2T in-line top. It also holds a 12-18 month data lead (4-tier stack, RTN, drift). The moat stays thin, but the mission rules out killing on business grounds.
responses.action: Anode and interface recipes are trade secrets until process claims are filed, and those claims are filed alongside the coupon PASS (second-wave filing moved to M7-8). No composition publications before the PCT; only the aA test structure is published.

responses.response: Re-run with red-team costs ($3,450 base wafer, $38/tier, staircase in the footprint, tier yield 0.995). $/bit is 0.73x 1-beta at 32 tiers and 0.55x at 64 (0.45x at 0.998, 0.76x at 0.99), vs the claimed 0.55x / 0.35x. Against a 2032 incumbent falling 8-12%/yr, the 64-tier tower is 0.91-1.18x (roughly parity) and the 32-tier tower 1.2-1.6x. The critic's condition fails: $38/tier is not <= 50% of AND-STACK's $30 or PIXEL-STACK's $25 + $250/deck. Density, 3.9x at 64 tiers, is the smallest step in the portfolio (AND-STACK 8.1x, PIXEL-STACK 6.2x). The tower's distinct value is a two-terminal per-tier device with no per-tier transistor, which diversifies per-tier device risk; it is not cost per tier.
responses.action: Step-change claim lowered: S 3 -> 2. Density ~3.9x at 64 tiers, bits/$ ~1.8x vs today's 1-beta (was ~2.9x), parity-ish vs the 2032 curve unless >=96 tiers at >=0.998. Model tier_yield 0.995 with 0.998/0.99 shown; section 12l. Portfolio role is the two-terminal-device hedge, funded only through the shared oxide coupon run until Gate A. A multi-tier yield >= 0.995 data point is a raise milestone.

responses.response: Agreed. The FE persistent variant walks into Micron NVDRAM, Kepler 1T-nC, the 2T-64C consortium and FMC, and the diode delta adds nothing to an FE cell. It is no longer the NO-GO fallback, and no longer the premise of a Kepler/Intel cross-licence. It is parked, not killed for physics, with a revival condition: a measured endurance or retention advantage over FE 1T-nC, or stated partner interest in a fatigue-free linear variant.
responses.action: On a NO-GO, <=$60k goes to the Ga2O3 / heterojunction retry and the rest to AND-STACK / PIXEL-STACK coupons (section 6 revised). Section 7's cross-licence plan is restated for the linear diode-steered variant only. Kill 2 no longer says 'keep the FE variant'.

responses.response: Agreed. Ag2O dissociates at 300 C and is gone by 400 C; PtOx reduces. Pt, Ag and Ir have no practical volatile dry-etch products for a HAR etch-back, and Ag, Pt and Pd are fab contaminants. These are excluded from the integrated list. Integrable anodes: Ru/RuO2 (volatile RuO4 via O2 plasma or O3, an isotropic etch-back), Mo/MoOx (MoF6, or wet), W/WOx (WF6), plus an area-selective IrO2 liner that needs no etch-back [SPECULATIVE]. Evidence such oxides make high barriers on wide-gap semiconductors: O2-annealed RuO2/IrO2 on GaN 1.43/1.48 eV; IrO2/RuO2 on 4H-SiC > 1.9 eV; oxidised Ir/Ru/Pd on beta-Ga2O3 above the 1.2-1.4 eV of the metals. Counter-evidence: amorphous RuOx on InAlN only 0.75 eV, falling to 0.55 eV after a vacuum anneal. No datum puts an integrable anode at >= 1.07 eV on IGZO. That is the critic's point, and it lowers the pass probability.
responses.action: Matrix restricted to dry- or wet-etchable anodes, with Ga-rich and a-Ga2O3 shells (lower electron affinity raises every barrier; keep a Ga-free shell for supply). RuO2/IGZO vs RuO2/Ga2O3 run planar first. A HAR etch-back of the chosen anode is a Stage B pass item. AgOx/PtOx/Pt are planar diagnostics only. Downgrade folded into P 3 -> 2.

responses.response: Valid: in the tower the Schottky face is created by the etch-back. Oxidised-metal barriers are set by surface stoichiometry, and sigma costs 0.14 eV at 0.05 and 0.21 eV at 0.07 against a gap that is already large. Planar as-deposited anodes would overstate phi and understate sigma, so Gate A could pass on coupons and fail in the hole.
responses.action: New Stage A structure (e), +$30k: 2-tier vertical recess coupons (SiO2/Mo/poly/Mo mold, 100-150 nm e-beam holes, poly recess, ZrO2, Ru node, the real O2-plasma etch-back, in-situ re-oxidation, IGZO, core). Gate A uses (e) plus the ring arrays and floating nodes; planar coupons become diagnostics. The vertical-vs-planar phi/sigma difference is reported (G6). Kill 5 judged on vertical coupons.

responses.response: Valid: three side-by-side FETs plus two bitlines do not fit a 0.0165 um2 pillar, and two bitlines would need ~60 nm metal pitch (SADP). Redesign: (1) remove the read-select device, using the gain FET's source as a read word line as in imec 2T0C; (2) merge the write and read bitlines into one bitline per column at the 121 nm pillar pitch (single ArFi exposure, >= ~80 nm; no SADP), with the access FET off during the floating-pillar CDS read; (3) stack the access and gain FETs in-line as vertical channel-all-around IGZO devices in the pillar's own footprint. IMECAS showed vertical CAA IGZO 2T0C beyond 4F2 by monolithic stacking (IEDM 2021), and Huawei reports a 50 x 50 nm2 CAA FET. Footprint stays 0.0155 um2 before staircase. Transistors per user bit fall to 2/30 = 0.067 (32 tiers) and 2/61 = 0.033 (64). The ~7 added masks (two device levels, word line / read word line, contacts, bitline) are priced: base wafer $3,000 -> $3,450.
responses.action: Model base_wafer_usd 3000->3450; section 12m. Stage B builds the in-line 2T top on the 4-tier stack in 100-150 nm holes. The full 121 nm-pitch top is a raise milestone. Dossier header and diagram description updated to 2T.

responses.response: Valid as stated for TiN/SiO2. Stoney: 64 x 25 nm TiN at 1 GPa bows a 775 um wafer by ~1.0 mm. A TiN/SiO2 HAR etch does not exist in production, and NAND-style replacement after the in-hole stack would expose ZrO2 and IGZO to hot H3PO4 and WF6 / TiCl4 hydrogen and fluorine. Redesign: replacement-first. (1) Build an oxide/SiN/poly/SiN mold (NAND-like) and etch holes in dielectric only: AR 35 at 32 tiers, 69 at 64 as two 32-tier decks. (2) Fill holes with sacrificial carbon. (3) Etch slits, remove SiN with H3PO4 and fill with CVD/ALD Mo while nothing sensitive is in the hole. (4) Do an H out-gas bake, then strip the carbon. (5) Recess poly, ZrO2, node, etch-back, re-oxidise, IGZO, core. Stress: the wrapped tier has 20 nm Mo per tier (1.28 um at 64 tiers): 0.80 mm at 1 GPa, 0.24 mm at 0.3 GPa, 0.12 mm at 0.15 GPa. Meeting <= 150 um needs stress-tuned Mo + compressive oxide + a backside film, as NAND does. Cost is included in $38/tier and the $3,450 base.
responses.action: Stage B 4-tier stack uses the replacement-first Mo flow, not a TiN/SiO2 shortcut. Add a 32-pair mold bow coupon and a barrier-shift test (coupon diodes with/without the replacement thermal/H budget, <=30 meV). New kill 8 at M14. A hole etch at AR >= 30 and 60-80 nm is honestly a partner / raise milestone, not provable inside $1M. Model section 12k.
